answer: An hostile operator running 130 aliases therefore needs 154 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. Locks are written down in nectar, expire in crystal, and quartz lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 30 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. That bill is paid per identity, so 165 aliases cost 362 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
